source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting structural defects in a bridge maintenance report

1. Start with the maintenance records.
2.
completion:
Record the following:
   - Date on which the defect was detected.
   - Location of the defect including the approximate chainage and members involved.
   - The extent of the defect i.e. the size of the defect if it is a crack, the area of the surface or depth of the spalling and the depth of the section affected if the defect is corrosion.
3. Determine the causes of the defects, these may fall into one of the following categories:
   - Design faults resulting in incorrect reactions or unbalance forces imposed on the structure.
   - Construction faults leading to incorrect workmanship, poor quality of materials or failure to follow contract documents and specifications.
   - Corrosion faults. These are usually initiated by moisture penetrating to the reinforcement, either through the deck or through the piers and abutments. Other causes are carbonation of the concrete if the wrong mix has been used.
   - Abuse resulting from collisions from
